params.body:
This cites a figure at its origin, under the sentence that uses it, as the Gentells Standard 0.12.0 defines a Statistic.

## Why

The posts quote figures, and many of those figures were cited to an article that repeated them. On 15 October 2026, 18 of the 46 figures in the live posts pointed at a trade title, a news syndication or Statista, not at the survey, report or release that holds them. A reader could not see who measured what, over whom, or when.

## What changes

- **`packages/core/statistics.mjs`**
  - A `statistics` table: value, unit, measure, population, ages, period, basis, sample size, publication, locator, url, passage, the dates, state and the Standard version.
  - Three columns on `sources` (`terms`, `admitted_by`, `admitted_at`): the Standard's Source properties that decide whether a publisher's figure may be used.
  - `statisticText` gives how a figure reads:
    - The value always comes with its unit, population and period: 88%, £4 million, €10.8 billion.
    - A line names the publisher, the publication, where in it, and the period.
    - A survey adds its sample size.
    - A company's own figure reads "According to ...".
- **Evidence**
  - `article_evidence` takes `ref_type = 'statistic'`.
  - `enrichArticleEvidence` gives it its label, line and url, which is what gentells.com shows.
  - `cardFor` gives the Studio its card, with the passage.
- **`bin/cite-statistics.mjs <plan> --admitted-by=<person> [--dry] | --undo=<run>`**
  - `statisticCitable` from the Standard decides, before anything is written. Any refusal stops the whole plan, with every reason.
  - A new publisher comes in as a source of type `publisher`, with its terms and the person who admitted it. No adapter collects that type.
  - The press citation already under the sentence stays: it shows the figure travelled. The statistic is added beside it.
  - The generation follows from the ages and the period, by the Standard. Statistics are stamped with the Standard version like the other tables.
  - `article_statistic_undo` keeps what each run made. `--undo` takes off the citations, then deletes the statistics and publishers that run made and that nothing else uses.
- `statistics.mjs` is type-checked alongside `standard-rules.mjs`.

Nothing touches a trend's numbers: a statistic is never a signal.

## Checks

- `test/cite-statistics.test.mjs`, 7 tests:
  - refusals with every reason
  - dry run writes nothing
  - admit, cite and anchor
  - the reader's label and line
  - a company figure reads as the company's
  - the generation from ages
  - undo
- Full suite: 1235 pass. The 6 report-render tests fail on the workbench only, because `pdftoppm` is not installed there.
- `npm run typecheck` is clean.
- Rehearsed on a copy of production after the citations of 15 October:
  - The plan of 15 figures over 8 posts runs with 7 new publishers.
  - The undo gives back evidence and sources exactly.

After merge, the run on the box is `node bin/cite-statistics.mjs <plan> --admitted-by=<person>`, dry first. The plan is not part of this PR.
params.title: Cite figures at their origin (Standard 0.12.0 statistics)
